genre: First-person survival horror with exploration and slow, heavy combat

setting.place: Remote island off the coast of Alaska
setting.premise: A weeklong camping trip goes wrong. The player is Tracey, an addict trying to save her kidnapped friends from a cult that will sacrifice them at the end of the week. Each night the island's terrain reshapes and the player must reach shelter before 3 a.m.
setting.cultural_layer: Orthodox Christian iconography from the first Russian settlers of Alaska, overlaid with pagan and demonic symbolism

art_direction.silhouettes: Simple models, strongly defined silhouettes so enemies are readable in darkness
art_direction.palette: Cold, high contrast. Green, grey, brown. Punk / grunge / acid accents

design_pillars: Combat is crude, slow and heavy. Every fight is a decision, not a reflex.
Sound carries information. Enemies are identified by audio signature before they are seen.
Show, do not tell. Narrative arrives through sparse dialogue and environment, never exposition.
Darkness is claustrophobic. Light sources are limited and consumable.
Inventory is constrained. Carrying one thing means not carrying another.

Wolf.movement: Roams the island freely, usually in packs
Wolf.attack: Circles the player, then closes in with bites
Wolf.defense: Breaks off and returns to circling when struck. Flees and resumes roaming if damaged enough

Stone totem.movement: Static while observed. Closes distance only when the player looks away. Placed near altars or standing water
Stone totem.attack: Passive aura. Player speed and stamina drop with proximity
Stone totem.defense: None. Breaks after a few hits

Furman.movement: Found sleeping or roaming in plains and forest
Furman.attack: Berserker charge into heavy bites. The charge itself induces fear
Furman.defense: No tactics, high health. Heavy blows stun it for several seconds

Cultist (Priest).movement: Stays near altars and fires. Can be summoned by spotters
Cultist (Priest).attack: Crossbow and poisoned blowdarts that induce hallucination
Cultist (Priest).defense: Fights at range. Repositions in a zigzag when attacked if allies are nearby

Cultist (Zealot).movement: Quiet, black attire, hides in darkness. Moves only when unobserved, then charges once spotted
Cultist (Zealot).attack: Knives, scythes, Molotovs. Fatal from behind
Cultist (Zealot).defense: Low health. Stealth is its defense

Cultist (Spotter).movement: Patrols cautiously with lamps, or gathers at altars and buildings
Cultist (Spotter).attack: Shotgun or club. Whistle or flare gun alerts and spawns reinforcements

hard_constraints: Nothing may reference technology that did not exist in 1978. No digital displays, no electronics beyond period radios, lamps, flashlights and telescopes.
No enemy may have a ranged instant-kill. Combat must always leave the player a decision.
Enemy behaviour must be expressible as a finite state machine over: idle, perceive, pursue, attack, recover, lose target, die.
No new enemy archetype family may be invented. New entities must be a variant of an existing archetype or an environmental hazard.
Every entity must be readable by silhouette and by audio signature alone.
Item names and flavour text use plain, period-appropriate American English. No fantasy nomenclature.
day_one_scene_list: 05 The forest road to the Glade
dialogue_presentation: Plain white subtitles in the style of the early Silent Hill games. Sparse. Never expository.
objective_ui: The current objective appears in the pause menu on a psychiatric intake form titled "How are you feeling today?" with a smiley face.
